## The Speed-Quality Paradox

A role that stays open has a cost to the business, and rushing to fill it risks a mis-hire, which has its own cost. The solution is not hiring faster for its own sake. It is removing waste from the process. We quote no averages or cost ranges here, because we have not cited a source for any. Measure your own.

### Where Time Gets Wasted

Map your own process and time each stage. These are the stages where delay commonly builds up:

| Stage | What commonly causes delay | What helps |
|---|---|---|
| Requisition approval | Slow sign-off loops | Pre-approved headcount |
| Job posting creation | Writing from scratch | Ready templates |
| Initial sourcing | Starting only after approval | An ongoing pipeline |
| Resume screening | Unstructured review | Structured criteria |
| Interview scheduling | Back-and-forth over availability | Self-service scheduling |
| Interview rounds | Too many rounds | Fewer, focused rounds |
| Decision making | Waiting for schedules to align | A standing decision group |
| Offer preparation | Starting from a blank page | Pre-built offer templates |

### 10 Tactics to Shorten the Process

#### 1. Pre-Approved Requisitions

Work with finance to pre-approve headcount for the quarter and avoid the approval loop.

#### 2. Evergreen Job Templates

Keep ready-to-post templates for recurring roles. Customize in minutes, not days.

#### 3. Always-On Sourcing Pipeline

Do not wait for a requisition to start sourcing. Maintain warm talent pools by role family.

#### 4. Structured Resume Screening

Use structured screening criteria and scoring so applications can be reviewed consistently and quickly. Keep a person responsible for the decision.

#### 5. Self-Service Interview Scheduling

Scheduling tools remove the back-and-forth. Candidates pick from available slots.

#### 6. Compressed Interview Formats

Replace long, many-round processes with a focused three-step process:

- A short phone screen
- A skills assessment
- A team and fit conversation

#### 7. Prompt Interviewer Feedback

Require scorecards soon after each interview. Delayed feedback delays decisions.

#### 8. Standing Offer Committee

Designate decision-makers in advance so you do not wait for schedules to align.

#### 9. Pre-Built Offer Packages

Work with HR and legal to create templated offers by role level. Customize specifics, not frameworks.

#### 10. Prompt Verbal Offers

When you find the right candidate, extend a verbal offer soon after the final interview, followed by the written offer.
